title: Operator backplane degraded-mode and offline safepath playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the operator backplane degraded-mode and offline safepath for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It documents detection signals, automated mitigation, step-by-step operator procedures, safe rollback/upgrade options for model and runtime swaps while the control backplane is partially or fully unavailable, and post-incident evidence collection for compliance. This is intended for field operators, SREs, and on-call engineers executing day-2 operations when backplane connectivity to control plane services is impaired.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: private deployments where the operator-control backplane (control-plane RPCs, artifact registry access, telemetry uplinks) is degraded due to network partition, WAN outage, or ingress/egress filtering.
- Audience: on-call operator, field engineer, platform SRE, and customer-facing operations. Not intended for routine maintenance.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Keep tenant inference traffic running with safe degradation of features (rollouts, telemetry) where necessary.
  - Provide a deterministic offline safepath to allow model rollbacks and emergency failovers without requiring full control-plane connectivity.
  - Preserve customer data integrity, audit evidence, and the ability to reconcile after recovery.
- Non-goals:
  - This playbook does not cover complete architectural rework or hardware RMA.
  - It does not replace scheduled maintenance procedures.

Quick decision guide (operator cheat-sheet):
1) Is the backplane partially available (control RPCs successfully reach at least 2/3 control endpoints)? If YES, prefer automated canary rollback via control-plane command.
2) If backplane is partially unavailable but local artifact store reachable, execute local-model-swap safepath (section: Local model swap).
3) If fully offline, use emergency offline-safepath with local signed artifacts and operator manual validation (section: Offline safepath).
4) In all cases, preserve evidence bundle prior to destructive actions (section: Evidence & telemetry preservation).

Signals and thresholds (what to monitor):
- Primary signals:
  - Control RPC success rate < 60% for > 2 minutes per region.
  - Artifact registry pull failure rate >= 20% for 5 minutes.
  - Heartbeat lag > 30s for operator agents.
  - Telemetry uplink error spikes (5xx) > 10x baseline.
- SLO impact triggers:
  - P95 inference latency increase > 25% tied to control-plane timeouts => escalate to degraded-mode.
  - Request error rate increase > 1% absolute => begin safeguards.

Prerequisites (requirements matrix):
| Requirement | Minimum value | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Local artifact cache | 2 replicas local to runtime | allow offline model swaps |
| Signed artifact bundle | present | security verification offline |
| Operator SSH / field console access | available | operator safety operations |
| Telemetry ringbuffer retention | 1h local | evidence collection for postmortem |
| Fallback model variants | available | graceful degradation |

Runbook: Backplane degraded-mode (fast path)
Steps for partial control-plane availability (recommended):
1) Detect: Confirm control RPC success rate >= 30% but < 60% for 3m. Tag incident 'backplane-degraded'.
2) Rate-limit: Apply per-tenant ingress token bucket (burst=2x baseline; sustained qps cap 0.8x) to reduce control-plane pressure.
   - CLI: redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant <TENANT_ID> --qps 0.8 --burst 2
3) Route: Shift non-critical traffic to cheaper local model variant using runtime routing policy.
   - Example routing JSON:
     {"route": "tenants/<TENANT_ID>/models", "policy": "local-fallback", "weight": 1.0}
4) Canary rollback (if model causing failures): initiate a targeted 5% canary rollback via control-plane. If rollback commands fail for a single canary, escalate to section 'Local model swap'.

Local model swap (when control-plane commands fail but local artifacts are available)
Purpose: Safely switch serving runtime to a pre-provisioned, signed model variant without control-plane orchestration.
Preconditions: local artifact cache present, signed manifest available, operator console access.
Steps:
1) Verify signed manifest signature matches root-of-trust.
   - Command: sha256sum manifest.json && gpg --verify manifest.sig manifest.json
2) Validate artifact integrity and disk space: ls -lh /var/lib/redwood/artifacts && df -h /var/lib/redwood
3) Start local warmup on a single worker: /usr/local/bin/runtime --load-model /var/lib/redwood/artifacts/<MODEL_ID> --warmup 100
4) Run local health checks (see health-check list below). If health checks pass, update local router to point production traffic at new model process.
5) Observe latency and error rate for 10 minutes. If errors increase > 0.5% absolute, revert using the saved model checkpoint and contact opt-in control-plane team to reconcile.

Health-check list (local swap):
- gRPC readiness endpoint responds within 200ms.
- KV cache priming < 2s for 90% of keys.
- Sample inference latency p50 within expected profile.
- No OOM or GPU driver errors in dmesg for 30s.

Offline safepath (fully isolated control-plane)
When control-plane is unreachable from all operator agents. This requires higher caution and explicit authorization.
Authorization: Incident commander + customer admin consent (if required by contract). Document authorization in the incident ticket.
Steps:
1) Evidence snapshot: capture local telemetry ringbuffer (packets).
   - Command: dd if=/var/log/redwood/telemetry-ringbuf bs=1M count=64 | gzip > /tmp/evidence-$(date +%s).gz
2) Verify signed artifact manifest and offline signature chain.
3) Use operator-runner tool to perform model swap with signature enforcement: /opt/redwood/operator-runner swap-offline --tenant <TENANT_ID> --manifest /var/lib/redwood/artifacts/manifest.json --dry-run
4) If dry-run passes, execute with --execute and --evidence <outfile>. The operator-runner generates an audit bundle containing action hashes and signed operator key. Ensure the bundle is uploaded to the evidence store once connectivity returns.
5) Apply network policing to limit traffic to critical routes only: iptables ruleset or egress ACLs as per customer's policy. Record ACL IDs.

Rollback and upgrade safety patterns
- Prefer canary rollbacks controlled by control-plane when available.
- For offline rollbacks, ensure the previously active model artifact and signed checkpoint are retained and checksummed before swap.
- Avoid schema-changing model artifacts in offline swaps. If necessary, perform schema adaptation via local shim layer and document compatibility validation.

Evidence & telemetry preservation (compliance-critical)
Required steps before any destructive operation:
1) Save telemetry ringbuffers and local logs to at least two different storage locations (local encrypted disk + removable media or customer-provided storage).
2) Create an evidence bundle with the following files: system-time.txt, manifest.json, manifest.sig, runtime-health.txt, operator-action.log.
3) Record operator identity and approval time in human-readable form and signed by the operator GPG key.

Table: Evidence bundle contents
| Filename | Description | Retention |
|---|---|---:|
| system-time.txt | UTC timestamp snapshot | 7 years (enterprise customers) |
| manifest.json | artifact manifest used for swap | 7 years |
| manifest.sig | signature of manifest | 7 years |
| operator-action.log | operator-runner actions with hashes | 7 years |

Escalation and communication templates
- Pager duty: tag incident with 'control-backplane' and set 30min urgency window.
- Customer comms: Use template 'Customer-backplane-degraded' and include ETA for reconciliation and whether offline safepath was used.
- Internal slide: create a 1-slide brief with root cause hypotheses and immediate mitigation actions.

Post-incident reconciliation checklist
1) Reconnect control-plane and verify heartbeat to all operator agents.
2) Upload evidence bundles to central evidence store and link to ticket.
3) Re-run model registry reconciliation to ensure control-plane view matches runtime state: redwoodctl reconcile --tenant <TENANT_ID> --source-runtime
4) Run integrity audits for all artifacts swapped during the incident.
5) Schedule a follow-up runbook review within 3 business days and assign owners for any gaps found.

Ownership and contacts
- Playbook owner: Platform SRE (oncall-platform@redwood.com).
- Escalation: Runtime engineering lead (runtime-lead@redwood.com).
- Compliance evidence custodian: Security & Compliance team (evidence-custodian@redwood.com).

Appendix A — Useful commands & snippets
- Check control RPC success rate:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://control.local/health | jq .rpc_success_rate
- Export artifact manifest checksum:
  sha256sum /var/lib/redwood/artifacts/manifest.json > /tmp/manifest.sha256
- Run local dry-run swap (example):
  /opt/redwood/operator-runner swap-offline --tenant tenant-123 --manifest /var/lib/redwood/artifacts/manifest.json --dry-run

Appendix B — Safety constraints for operators
- Never perform destructive storage deletes while in offline safepath.
- If there is any doubt about artifact provenance, escalate to runtime-lead.
- Maintain an unbroken chain of custody for evidence bundles.
